commits.message: Route the stack profile refusal by the fragments the stack prints

Render the public node compose model from the stack's own node directory and env file

The containers test rendered the base compose file against the checkout's
untracked demo/midgard-node/.env, which CI does not have. The public stack
fixture now writes its env file into its node directory, as the stack
requires, and the test renders in that directory with that env file.

Add the preprod-testing fast-timer twin stack example and drill steps

The twin configuration runs one journey cycle on its own endpoint and DA
ports, so it can run beside the default stack from a separate worktree. The
testing-flow page lists the existing commands that prove the withdrawal
payout, operator bond recovery and the DA-bond withdraw on its short timers.

Run the preprod-rehearsal profile on the public stack route

The stack takes the public route for every Preprod production profile and
checks operators against the compiled profile's allow-list, so a
preprod-rehearsal stack loads with every public input check. Refusal
messages name the compiled profile. A preprod-rehearsal-stack test project
loads a rehearsal configuration against that profile's allow-list.

Tighten public release resume checks and mounted-file refusals

Reopening a placed public release now requires its provenance to equal the
provenance the stack completed, and a public stack checks its provenance
blueprint hash on every run. Mounted public files report size and permission
refusals separately, and mounted release JSON keeps the read refusal. The
out-of-band signing steps name the registry digest and the key file phase 1
reads. The public release tests share one fixture module and the container
checks move to their own file.
Match the intended refusal in the rehearsal profile tests

Complete the public release provenance from the deployed registry

A preprod-public operator cannot know the parameter registry digest before
initialize writes the registry, yet prerequisites demanded the registry
and a provenance carrying its digest. The operator now supplies the
provenance without evidence.parameterRegistryDigest. Phase 1 checks its
other fields against the .env revision and images and the compiled
profile, and that the release input names no registry but the stack's;
prerequisites check its blueprint hash against the blueprint they build.
Once the deployment has written its registry, the public-release step
writes the completed provenance once into the run directory, with a
release input naming it and the deployed registry. The public release and
the watcher release are both signed from that input. A resume reuses the
completed provenance and refuses one that no longer matches, and a
supplied digest that differs from the deployed registry is refused.

Tests cover a fresh public stack passing the prerequisite check without a
registry, the completed digest equal to the deployed registry's, a resume
and the watcher release reusing it, the phase-1 provenance refusals, and
an ingress subnet held by another Docker network. The public input
fixture moves to its own module.

Report why a mounted public file is refused

readMountedHttpFile replaced its own refusals (a secret file others can
read, an empty or oversized file) with the generic missing-or-unreadable
message, so an operator never learned what to fix. It now keeps them; a
missing or unreadable file still gets the generic message. File contents
never enter either.
Carry the release-age exemption into the boundary consumer

Add the preprod-rehearsal deployment profile

A Preprod profile for rehearsing the public deploy with low bonds. Every
value equals preprod-public's except the economics and the pooled DA bond
amounts, which equal preprod-testing's under its bounded-acceptance-v1
schedule, so maturity, dispute, operator shift and every DA window match
the public release while bonds stay cheap. preprod-testing stays the
selected profile and is unchanged.

The rehearsal is classed with the public profiles everywhere except
economics: the production allow-list and commit-event depth rules, the
retained-DA transport requirement, the public timing rules, release
provenance and watcher release authoring, the blueprint classification
registry, public HTTP/TLS listen, readiness and database-error redaction,
the opener margin, and the release image and blueprint-rebuild scripts.

The profile-name and profile-class tables move to
deployment-profile-names.mjs, and the generator now emits
PRODUCTION_DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE_NAMES so core, node and watcher read one
public-class helper instead of comparing names. The new module is listed
wherever the generator inputs are (CI paths, preflight FULL_RUN, traced
refusal inputs, the interactive emulator fixture).

The generated profile table's size cap rises to its new line count: it
holds one literal per profile.

Tests compare the loaded profiles rather than pinning numbers: the
rehearsal is preprod-public with preprod-testing's economics and DA bond,
is held to every production rule preprod-public is, and generates its own
Aiken environment.

Document the stack-signed public release

The preprod-public procedure now builds the profile first, signs the
release in the public-release step, and names the standalone
sign-deployment-release command only as the out-of-band alternative with
its real arguments. It describes the loopback host ports, the Postgres
password file, the ingress subnet, the new phase-1 refusals, and the
journey user and recipient funding. The node example uses the signed
release's file names.

Write public journey wallet seeds exclusively and delete them after use

A preprod-public journey writes each signing seed to a new 0600 file in
the run directory (exclusive create, replacing one an interrupted run left)
and deletes it when the deposit or withdrawal command ends, failed or not.

Sign the public release in the stack and harden the public inputs

The public-release step now signs the release for the finalized
deployment into public.releaseDirectory with the release input's key,
through the same code as sign-deployment-release, and opens it as public
listen does. It runs before runtime-configuration, which binds the signed
files; a rerun verifies the release already there and never signs again.
The stack and the standalone command share the program-commitments
derivation, so they sign the same release from the same input.

Phase 1 also refuses: a signing key the trust roots do not list, a release
directory without a parent or holding a partial release, a private file
owned by another user, a node database owned by another user (printing
the chown), an operator wallet off the allow-list, and a Docker network on
the ingress subnet. The deployed blueprint classification is its own
input, and the step refuses a release registry that classifies otherwise.

In public mode the node metrics and DA ports and Postgres bind to the
loopback, the node API too when the ingress fronts it, and Postgres reads
its password from a 0600 file instead of its environment. The example
prover and availability minimums cover the 10,000 ADA bond, collateral
and fees. The ingress config-text test is removed.

Refuse a stack whose profile differs from the compiled one

loadStackConfig, and so --check, now refuses an .env whose
MIDGARD_DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE is not the profile the checkout was compiled
for, printing the generate-and-build command that fixes it. A
preprod-testing stack accepts a ws:// endpoint again; only https:// is
refused for it.

Document the preprod-public deployment procedure

A new operator page gives the e2e-stack sequence for preprod-public:
inputs, Mithril-synced providers, reference scripts, init, operator,
the release-signing stop and resume, services and the acceptance
journey. It lists each wallet's funding from the profile parameters, the
watcher process fields and the remaining owner inputs. The stack
specification and the acceptance runbook name the public profile and the
public-release step.
